mainTopic: How many judges are needed for the case of מוציא שם רע, and two ways to explain the argument between רבי מאיר (three judges) and the חכמים (twenty-three judges)
overview: The משנה records an argument about a husband who slanders his wife (מוציא שם רע). רבי מאיר says three judges hear the case, and the חכמים say twenty-three. The גמרא finishes its first explanation: the witnesses warned her only about מלקות, not death. So the argument is really the known dispute between the רבנן (lashes need three judges) and רבי ישמעאל (lashes need twenty-three). רבינא then gives a different explanation: one of the husband's witnesses turned out to be a relative or פסול. To explain this, the גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא, who says the Torah mentions a 'third witness' so that he is treated just like the other two. From this רבי עקיבא learns that a helper in a מצוה is surely rewarded like the doer. He also learns that one bad witness cancels the testimony of the whole group, even a hundred. Finally, רבי יוסי limits that rule to capital cases. רבי says it applies to both kinds of cases, but only when the disqualified witnesses joined in the warning, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case: warned about lashes, not about death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes describing the case behind the argument. The witnesses warned her only about מלקות, not about the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where they warned her that she would get lashes, but they did not warn her that she would get the death penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that began earlier. It defines the exact case where רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue: she was warned only about lashes, so death is not on the table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can only be punished for a sin if they were warned about that specific punishment. Since she was warned only about מלקות, the most she can get is lashes. That turns the case into a 'lashes case', which sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They warned (from הַתְרָאָה, the warning given before a sin)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say adultery stops being a capital sin. It only says that in this particular case the warning covered only lashes, so only lashes can be given.

phrases.english: where they warned her about lashes,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from before. 'Her' is the wife her husband accused, even though the word looks masculine.

phrases.english: but did not warn her about death.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַתְרוֹ בַּיהּ מַלְקוֹת, וְלָא אַתְרוֹ בַּיהּ קַטְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an answer from the previous part of the daf, which explains the dispute in the משנה about מוציא שם רע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is one where only lashes, not death, can result, because the warning was only about lashes.

steps.title: The argument is really about how many judges give lashes
steps.stepSummary: With the case set as a 'lashes case', the גמרא says רבי מאיר and the חכמים follow the dispute between the רבנן (three judges for lashes) and רבי ישמעאל (twenty-three).
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue the same way as רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן argue, as the משנה teaches: Lashes are judged by three judges. In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said: by twenty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא links our argument to a known argument found in another משנה. Whoever needs three judges for lashes says three here, and whoever needs twenty-three says twenty-three here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the case can end only in lashes, the number of judges depends on the rule for lashes. רבי מאיר holds like the רבנן (three is enough), and the חכמים hold like רבי ישמעאל (twenty-three). So nobody has to invent a new idea; the argument fits a dispute we already know.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: First explanation: she was warned only about lashes, so the argument is the known dispute about whether lashes need three judges (רבנן) or twenty-three (רבי ישמעאל).

phrases.english: And they argue along the lines of the dispute
between רבי ישמעאל and the Rabbis,
as we learned: Lashes are judged by three.
In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said:
by twenty-three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the case just defined to show which known dispute it depends on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the argument to an existing dispute
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר holds like the רבנן that lashes need three judges; the חכמים hold like רבי ישמעאל that lashes need twenty-three.

steps.title: רבינא: one of the witnesses was a relative or disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רבינא offers a different case: one of the husband's witnesses turned out to be a relative or פסול. The argument then depends on a dispute between רבי יוסי and רבי about רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The case is where one of the witnesses was found to be a relative or disqualified. They argue along the lines of the dispute between רבי יוסי and רבי, according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a whole new way to explain the argument in the משנה. He changes the case to one where a group of witnesses includes one who is not allowed to testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether one bad witness ruins the testimony of the whole group. רבי עקיבא has a rule about this, and רבי יוסי and רבי argue about how far his rule reaches. רבינא says רבי מאיר and the חכמים split along that same line; the גמרא now quotes רבי עקיבא's source.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
For example, where one of the witnesses was found
to be a relative or disqualified,
and they argue along the lines of the dispute
between רבי יוסי and רבי,
according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּמְצָא אֶחָד מִן הָעֵדִים קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent explanation of the משנה's argument instead of the lashes explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument in the משנה depends on how far רבי עקיבא's rule about a disqualified witness in a group reaches.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the third witness is treated like the other two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה where רבי עקיבא teaches that the Torah mentions a third witness only to treat him as strictly as the first two.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי עקיבא says, the third witness was mentioned only to be strict with him, to make his law like these other witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי עקיבא's rule that רבינא just mentioned. The פסוק says 'two or three witnesses', and רבי עקיבא explains why 'three' is written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are already enough, so why mention three? רבי עקיבא says: so that a third witness counts fully as part of the group and is treated just like the first two. That is why one bad witness can affect the whole group.

keyTerms.meaning: Like these (the same as the other witnesses)

phrases.english: As we learned: רבי עקיבא says,
the third witness was mentioned only
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק 'by two witnesses or three witnesses', דברים 17:6.

phrases.english: to be strict with him,
to make his law like these others.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, לֹא בָּא שְׁלִישִׁי אֶלָּא לְהַחְמִיר עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the רבי עקיבא rule that רבינא's explanation depends on.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's rule that a third witness counts fully as part of the group
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה in מכות reading the פסוק in דברים 17:6

steps.title: If a helper in sin is punished, a helper in a מצוה is surely rewarded
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא draws a lesson: if the Torah punishes someone who just joins sinners like the sinners themselves, it surely rewards someone who joins a מצוה like the one doing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the Torah punishes someone who attaches himself to sinners like the sinners themselves. How much more so will God give reward to someone who attaches himself to those doing a מצוה like the one doing the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא is continuing his teaching and pulling out a moral lesson. This is a קל וחומר from punishment to reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third witness only 'joined' the other two, yet he gets their full punishment. Since God's goodness is greater than His punishment, someone who joins in a מצוה surely gets the full reward. This step adds a lesson about reward; it does not change the legal discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who attaches himself, a helper or tag-along
How much more so (sign of a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: the third witness is treated like the first two. And if a helper in sin gets full punishment, a helper in a מצוה surely gets full reward.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known lesson: even helping or joining someone else's מצוה earns full reward, like doing it yourself.

phrases.english: If so, the Torah punished
the one who attaches himself to sinners
like the sinners themselves –
how much more so
will He pay reward
to the one who attaches himself to a doer of a מצוה
like the one doing the מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן עָנַשׁ הַכָּתוּב אֶת הַנִּיטְפָּל לְעוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה כְּעוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי עקיבא's quoted teaching, drawing a קל וחומר from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who joins in doing a מצוה receives full reward like the main doer, by קל וחומר from the third witness who gets full punishment.

steps.title: One bad witness cancels the whole group, even a hundred
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא continues: just as one disqualified witness out of two cancels the testimony, so too one out of three, and even one out of a hundred, learned from the word 'עדים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: With two witnesses, if one turns out to be a relative or disqualified, their testimony is cancelled. So too with three: if one turns out to be a relative or disqualified, their testimony is cancelled. How do we know this is true even with a hundred witnesses? The פסוק says 'witnesses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting רבי עקיבא's teaching from the משנה. It gives a second lesson from the extra 'third witness' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two witnesses it is obvious: if one is disqualified, only one is left, and one witness is not enough. רבי עקיבא says a third witness is treated the same way, so one bad witness ruins the whole group even though two good ones remain. The plural word 'עדים' stretches this rule to any number of witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: A relative, who may not testify

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two good witnesses are 'enough' on their own. רבי עקיבא's point is that the whole group counts as one unit, so one bad member cancels everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule that רבינא's case in step 3 depends on: one of the husband's witnesses was a relative or פסול.

phrases.english: And just as with two witnesses,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל –
phrases.english: if one of them turns out to be a relative or disqualified –
their testimony is cancelled,
so too with three,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל –
phrases.english: if one of them turns out to be a relative or disqualified –
their testimony is cancelled.
And how do we know that this is true even with a hundred?
The פסוק says: 'Witnesses.'
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק as before, דברים 17:6, which says 'witnesses' even when talking about three.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה שְׁנַיִם, נִמְצָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן קָרוֹב אוֹ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same משנה of רבי עקיבא with a second lesson from the third witness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If any one witness in a group is a relative or פסול, the testimony of the entire group is cancelled, no matter how many witnesses there are.

steps.title: רבי יוסי limits the rule to capital cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says רבי עקיבא's rule applies only in דיני נפשות. In דיני ממונות, the testimony stands with the remaining valid witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: When does this rule apply? In capital cases. But in money cases, the testimony stands with the rest of the witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא brings the first side of the argument about how to understand רבי עקיבא. רבי יוסי says the rule is limited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, one bad witness cancels the whole group only when a life is at stake. In a money case, we simply ignore the disqualified witness and rely on the valid ones who remain.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (a way of limiting a rule)
Capital cases, where a life is at stake
With the rest (the remaining valid witnesses)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: He means רבי עקיבא's rule that one bad witness cancels the whole group.

phrases.english: In capital cases,
but in money cases
the testimony stands with the rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the dispute about how far רבי עקיבא's rule from step 6 reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One disqualified witness cancels the group only in דיני נפשות. In דיני ממונות, the remaining valid witnesses are accepted.

steps.title: רבי says the rule applies in both kinds of cases, but only when they warned
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that the rule applies to both money and capital cases, but only when the disqualified witnesses joined in warning the sinner. The end of his statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: This applies both to money cases and to capital cases. And when? When they warned them. But when they did not warn them,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second side of the argument. רבי gives a different limit than רבי יוסי, and his statement continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי does not split money cases from capital cases. Instead, the key question for him is whether the disqualified witnesses took part in the warning (התראה). If they did, they made themselves part of the group, and they cancel everyone. If they did not, the rule seems not to apply, and the end of that thought comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: They warned the sinner before the act (התראה)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two opinions. רבי יוסי's dividing line is money cases versus capital cases. רבי's dividing line is whether the disqualified witness warned or not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the dispute רבינא used in step 3 to explain the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת וְאֶחָד דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת,
phrases.english: Both money cases and capital cases,
And when?
When they warned them,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the relatives or disqualified witnesses, and 'them' are the sinners.

phrases.english: but when they did not warn them,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת וְאֶחָד דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יוסי from step 7 about how far רבי עקיבא's rule reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's rule applies in both money and capital cases, but only when the disqualified witnesses took part in warning the sinner.
